title: Waterfall-modulated $α$-attractors
comment: 24 pages, 15 figures
summary: Hybrid $α$-attractor models \cite{Kallosh:2022ggf} can have significantly greater values of $n_{s}$ and smaller $r$, while preserving the relation $r\cong 3α(1-n_s)^2$, which is valid for exponential T- and E-models at large values of the inflaton field. Here we study single-field $α$-attractors with features inspired by hybrid models: one can uplift the potential, and one can also have a waterfall regime that leads to a premature termination of inflation near the critical point $\varphi_c$. This allows one to increase the effective number of e-foldings $N_c$ in formulas like $n_s\simeq 1-{2\over N_c}$, $r\simeq {12 α\over N_c^2}$. By changing the waterfall's steepness and location, one can continuously move the predictions along the curves with $r\cong 3α(1-n_s)^2$ as $n_s$ increases and $r$ decreases. We also study the effect of waterfall insertions and uplift on $n_s$ in quintessential $α$-attractors that describe inflation and dynamical dark energy.

AI.tldr: This paper studies single-field α-attractors with hybrid-model-inspired features (potential uplift and a waterfall regime) that can enhance the effective number of e-foldings, thereby increasing the spectral index n_s and decreasing the tensor-to-scalar ratio r, while keeping the relation r ≅ 3α(1-n_s)^2. The work also examines effects of waterfall insertions and uplift on n_s in quintessential α-attractors for inflation and dark energy.
AI.motivation: Hybrid α-attractor models can produce larger n_s and smaller r while preserving the characteristic α-attractor relation r ≅ 3α(1-n_s)^2, motivating a detailed study of how such features modify predictions. The goal is to understand how uplifting the potential and adding a waterfall regime affect inflationary observables and the effective number of e-foldings.
AI.method: The authors study single-field α-attractors modified with hybrid-inspired features: a potential uplift and a waterfall regime leading to premature termination of inflation near a critical point φ_c. By tuning the waterfall's steepness and location, predictions are moved continuously along curves with the fixed relation r ≅ 3α(1-n_s)^2. The approach also extends to quintessential α-attractors describing both inflation and dynamical dark energy.
AI.result: The uplift and waterfall regime allow an increase in the effective number of e-foldings N_c in formulas such as n_s ≃ 1 - 2/N_c and r ≃ 12α/N_c^2. Varying the waterfall's steepness and location continuously shifts predictions toward higher n_s and lower r along the curves preserving r ≅ 3α(1-n_s)^2. Effects on n_s from waterfall insertions and uplift in quintessential α-attractors are also quantified.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid-inspired features in α-attractor models provide a mechanism to continuously adjust inflationary predictions (higher n_s, lower r) along the characteristic α-attractor relation, and similar effects apply to quintessential α-attractors coupling inflation to dynamical dark energy.

title: X-ray signals converted from high-frequency gravitational waves emitted by spinning light primordial black hole dark matter
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure
summary: We investigate the detectability of high-frequency gravitational waves from the superradiance of light primordial black hole dark matter through photons converted in the Galactic magnetic field. We find that the signal is significantly enhanced in the X-ray frequency range around $10^{18}$Hz. For clustered initial conditions, future X-ray observations may detect the converted photons from primordial black holes in the mass range $10^{-15}M_{\odot} \sim 10^{-13}M_{\odot}$. Our results indicate that future X-ray observations could provide a new probe of light primordial black hole dark matter through high-frequency gravitational waves.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates detecting high-frequency gravitational waves generated by superradiance from light primordial black hole dark matter, which are converted into photons in the Galactic magnetic field. The signal is enhanced in the X-ray frequency range (~10^18 Hz), and future X-ray observations could detect converted photons from primordial black holes with masses between 10^-15 to 10^-13 solar masses for clustered initial conditions, providing a new probe of light PBH dark matter.
AI.motivation: To explore a new avenue for detecting light primordial black hole dark matter through high-frequency gravitational waves, which are otherwise difficult to observe directly.
AI.method: The authors analyze the detectability of high-frequency gravitational waves produced via superradiance from light primordial black holes, focusing on photon conversion in the Galactic magnetic field, and evaluate the signal enhancement in the X-ray band.
AI.result: The signal is significantly enhanced in the X-ray frequency range around 10^18 Hz, and for clustered initial conditions, future X-ray observations may detect converted photons from PBHs in the mass range 10^-15 to 10^-13 solar masses.
AI.conclusion: Future X-ray observations could serve as a new probe of light primordial black hole dark matter through high-frequency gravitational waves.

title: Cosmic Structures in CDM and SIDM
comment: 34 pages, 5 figures. Invited review for "One Hundred and Ten Years of General Relativity: Reviews and Perspectives". Accepted for publication in IJMPD
summary: The standard $Λ$ Cold Dark Matter ($Λ$CDM) model has achieved remarkable success in explaining the formation and evolution of cosmic structures on large scales, supported by a wide range of observations, including the cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure surveys, and galaxy clusters. However, discrepancies between theoretical predictions and observations on small scales, have motivated the exploration of alternative dark matter models, including the self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) scenario. This review provides an overview of the theoretical foundations of CDM structure formation, the small-scale challenges, and the solutions proposed within the SIDM framework. We summarize recent theoretical developments in the SIDM framework and discuss current observational constraints on the dark matter self-interaction cross-section with particular emphasis on galaxy clusters.

AI.tldr: A review of the self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) paradigm as a solution to small-scale challenges facing the standard ΛCDM model, summarizing theoretical developments and observational constraints on the dark matter self-interaction cross-section, with particular focus on galaxy clusters.
AI.motivation: While ΛCDM successfully explains large-scale cosmic structure, discrepancies between theory and observations on small scales motivate exploring alternative dark matter models, including the SIDM scenario.
AI.method: A review summarizing the theoretical foundations of CDM structure formation, analyzing small-scale challenges, surveying recent theoretical developments in the SIDM framework, and compiling current observational constraints on the dark matter self-interaction cross-section, especially from galaxy clusters.
AI.result: Provides an overview of solutions proposed within the SIDM framework and summarizes current observational constraints on the dark matter self-interaction cross-section, with emphasis on galaxy clusters.
AI.conclusion: SIDM offers a viable alternative to ΛCDM for resolving small-scale discrepancies while preserving its large-scale successes, with galaxy clusters providing important observational constraints on the self-interaction cross-section.

title: Forecast for the detectability of patchy hydrogen reionization in WEAVE-QSO measurements of the Lyman-$α$ forest power spectrum at redshift $z \geq 4$
comment: 15 pages, 13 figures, 1 table, submitted to MNRAS
summary: We present the first detailed forecasts for the detectability of patchy hydrogen reionization in the one-dimensional Ly$α$ forest power spectrum to be measured by the WEAVE-QSO survey. Using the Sherwood-relics reionization simulations and a WEAVE-QSO survey configuration, we generate mock spectra in four redshift bins, $z=4.0,4.2,4.4,$ and $4.6$, in which relic ionization and temperature fluctuations from patchy hydrogen reionization enhance the Ly$α$ forest power spectrum on large scales (i.e., at wavenumber $k\sim 10^{-3},\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$). Our Ly$α$ forest pipeline forecasts the power spectrum covariance by considering sample size, spectral resolution, noise subtraction, continuum placement, metal contamination, and damping wings from high-column density absorbers. Applying our covariance forecast within a Bayesian parameter inference framework, we find that the signature of patchy hydrogen reionization should be detectable at a significance of $\simeq 4.5σ$. The forthcoming WEAVE-QSO 1D power spectrum measurements should therefore be able to directly detect and characterize the large-scale relic imprint of patchy hydrogen reionization in the Ly$α$ forest power spectrum at $z\geq 4$.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first detailed forecasts for detecting patchy hydrogen reionization in the 1D Lyα forest power spectrum using the WEAVE-QSO survey. Using Sherwood-relics simulations and WEAVE-QSO survey configuration, mock spectra are generated at four redshift bins (z=4.0-4.6). A power spectrum covariance forecast accounts for sample size, spectral resolution, noise subtraction, continuum placement, metal contamination, and damping wings. Bayesian parameter inference predicts the patchy reionization signature should be detectable at ~4.5σ significance at large scales (k~10⁻³ s km⁻¹), meaning WEAVE-QSO can directly detect and characterize the relic imprint of patchy hydrogen reionization at z≥4.
AI.motivation: The goal is to forecast whether the WEAVE-QSO survey can detect the large-scale relic signatures of patchy hydrogen reionization in the 1D Lyα forest power spectrum at z≥4, where ionization and temperature fluctuations from reionization enhance the power spectrum on large scales.
AI.method: The authors use Sherwood-relics reionization simulations combined with a WEAVE-QSO survey configuration to generate mock Lyα forest spectra at z=4.0, 4.2, 4.4, and 4.6. A power spectrum pipeline forecasts the covariance by accounting for sample size, spectral resolution, noise subtraction, continuum placement, metal contamination, and damping wings from high-column density absorbers. The covariance forecast is applied within a Bayesian parameter inference framework to assess detectability.
AI.result: The signature of patchy hydrogen reionization is predicted to be detectable at a significance of approximately 4.5σ in the large-scale (k~10⁻³ s km⁻¹) Lyα forest power spectrum at z≥4.
AI.conclusion: WEAVE-QSO 1D power spectrum measurements should be able to directly detect and characterize the large-scale relic imprint of patchy hydrogen reionization in the Lyα forest power spectrum at z≥4.

title: The Ĝ Infrared Search for Extraterrestrial Civilizations with Large Energy Supplies. V. When Galaxies Glow with Industry
comment: 34 pages, 16 figures, 4 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We present the most robust stellar population synthesis (SPS)-based search for galaxy-spanning technological waste heat to date, applied to 129 nearby galaxies spanning a wide range of spectral energy distribution (SED) types, including ultraluminous IR galaxies and MIR-luminous active galactic nuclei (AGN). We incorporate the AGENT Dyson sphere formalism into the Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis code at the stellar population level, so nebular and dust emission respond self-consistently to Dyson sphere reprocessing. With \texttt{Prospector}, we perform a suite of 1,419 injection recovery tests across a range of covering fractions, $α$, where we successfully recover the injected covering fractions (best-fit slope $m = 0.92$) and detect them through Bayesian model selection down to $α\sim 4$--$5\%$ in quiescent galaxies. None of our 129 galaxies prefer a Dyson sphere component, and we place the first per-galaxy 95\% upper limits on warm ($T_{\rm BB} \gtrsim 100$K) swarms, reaching a median $α< 0.3\%$ across quiescent hosts without a dominant AGN. Our injection-calibrated detection rates convert these zero detections into a population bound of $<2.6\%$ of galaxies hosting $α= 25\%$ swarms ($95\%$ confidence). Because survey colors cannot separate waste heat from starbursts and AGN, we develop a scaffold for future searches, running from inexpensive archival screens such as the Balmer decrement and the stellar-to-dynamical-mass offset a swarm leaves behind, through resolved fitting with nuclear excision, to PRIMA FIR photometry that makes targeted JWST imaging decisive. We find that the outskirts of quiescent galaxies are the best hunting grounds for future technosignature searches.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the most robust SPS-based search for galaxy-spanning Dyson sphere waste heat to date, applied to 129 nearby galaxies. Using injection recovery tests, they find no galaxy prefers a Dyson sphere component and place the first per-galaxy 95% upper limits on warm swarms (median α < 0.3%), converting zero detections into a population bound of <2.6% of galaxies hosting α=25% swarms. They develop a hierarchical scaffold for future searches, identifying quiescent galaxy outskirts as the best hunting grounds.
AI.motivation: To search for galaxy-spanning technological waste heat (Dyson spheres) using robust stellar population synthesis techniques across a diverse sample of nearby galaxies, and to establish calibrated upper limits and a practical framework for future technosignature searches.
AI.method: Incorporates the AGENT Dyson sphere formalism into the Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis (FSPS) code at the stellar population level so nebular and dust emission respond self-consistently to Dyson sphere reprocessing. Uses Prospector to perform 1,419 injection recovery tests across covering fractions, applies Bayesian model selection to 129 nearby galaxies spanning ultraluminous IR galaxies and MIR-luminous AGN, and develops a multi-tier search scaffold from archival screens to resolved fitting to JWST observations.
AI.result: Injection recovery tests successfully recover covering fractions (slope m=0.92) down to α~4-5% in quiescent galaxies. None of the 129 galaxies prefer a Dyson sphere component. Median upper limit of α<0.3% for quiescent hosts without dominant AGN. Population bound of <2.6% of galaxies hosting α=25% swarms at 95% confidence.
AI.conclusion: Zero detections of Dyson spheres across the sample establish strong population-level constraints on galaxy-spanning technological waste heat. The outskirts of quiescent galaxies are identified as the most promising targets for future technosignature searches, and a practical multi-tier observational scaffold is provided to make them decisive.

title: Cosmography with DESI-DR1 Cosmic Chronometers: Direct H(z) measurements from Luminous Red Galaxy ages
comment: 14 main text pages (7 figures), 4 appendix pages (6 figures). Supplementary material will be provided in the journal version of the article, currently under correction
summary: Providing robust redshift estimates for almost 3 million luminous red galaxies (LRGs), the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) offers a unique opportunity to test the expansion rate of the Universe with independent approaches. We apply the cosmic chronometer method to derive new, independent constraints on the Hubble parameter at 0.3<z<1.2 from the differential age evolution of DESI LRGs. We select spectra applying spectroscopic cuts to ensure sample purity and remove contamination by star-forming objects, then build a robust sample of cosmic chronometers (CCs) by stacking to obtain stable, high signal-to-noise (S/N) spectra, which also serves as a democratic binning choice for the $t-z$ plane. Ages are estimated by measuring Lick indices on the stacked spectra and fitting them with a theoretical stellar population model. We obtain $t-z$ relations from which we derive $H(z)$ constraints via two independent approaches: a fit with a pivotal-redshift cosmography, and a direct estimate from the original CC method. The cosmographic fit yields posteriors for the kinematic parameters $\{H_{z_0}, q_{z_0}, j_{z_0}\}$ compatible with currently considered cosmologies, giving a precision-level estimate of $H(z)$. We provide the maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) $H(z)$ estimate, an array of the median confidence region in the $H-z$ plane, and its covariance matrix. We also leverage the redshift distributions of the $t-z$ relation for different velocity dispersion groups to obtain two independent local measurements using the discrete approximation $H(z) \approx -Δz/[Δt (1+z)]$; the one from the reddest envelope of CCs gives $H(z \approx 0.61) = 88.5^{+6.7}_{-12.6}$ (stat.) $\pm 8.1$ (syst.) km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Systematic uncertainties for both the cosmographic and discrete $H(z)$ measurements come from a comprehensive analysis of all methodological choices in the data treatment.

AI.tldr: Using DESI luminous red galaxies as cosmic chronometers, the authors derive new constraints on the Hubble parameter H(z) at 0.3<z<1.2 by estimating galaxy ages from Lick indices on stacked spectra, yielding H(z≈0.61)=88.5^{+6.7}_{-12.6} (stat.) ±8.1 (syst.) km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, consistent with current cosmologies.
AI.motivation: DESI provides ~3 million LRGs with robust redshifts, offering a unique opportunity to independently test the expansion rate of the Universe using the cosmic chronometer method, a model-independent approach to constraining H(z).
AI.method: Select LRG spectra with spectroscopic cuts for purity, stack them to build high signal-to-noise cosmic chronometer samples, estimate ages via Lick indices fitted with stellar population models, then derive H(z) from the t-z relation using two approaches: a cosmographic fit with pivotal redshift yielding kinematic parameters {H, q, j}, and the discrete cosmic chronometer approximation H(z)≈-Δz/[Δt(1+z)].
AI.result: The cosmographic fit yields kinematic parameters {H_z0, q_z0, j_z0} compatible with current cosmologies. The discrete method on the reddest envelope yields H(z≈0.61)=88.5^{+6.7}_{-12.6} (stat.) ±8.1 (syst.) km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹. Systematic uncertainties are derived from a comprehensive analysis of all methodological choices in data treatment.
AI.conclusion: The study provides new, independent H(z) constraints from DESI LRGs as cosmic chronometers, with results consistent with standard cosmologies, and releases the MAP H(z) estimate, median confidence region in the H-z plane, and its covariance matrix for future use.

title: Recycled Gas Dominates the Metal-rich Fuel of Supermassive Black Holes
comment: 14 pages, 1 table, 4 figures
summary: Understanding the origin and chemical properties of gas accreted by supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is essential for linking black hole growth to galaxy evolution. Using a suite of 30 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations, we investigate the chemical properties of gas accreted onto SMBHs in massive galaxies with stellar masses of $10^{10.9-11.9}\,\rm M_\odot$ and black hole masses of $10^{8.5-9.7}\,\rm M_\odot$ at $z=0$. By tracing the full cosmological histories of individual gas particles, we identify their origins and enrichment pathways. The accreted gas is classified into four categories: ``early'' gas accreted during the early assembly phase of the main halo, ``external'' gas originating from other galaxies or subhalos, ``recycled'' gas enriched through stellar evolution processes within the primary galaxy, including asymptotic giant branch (AGB) winds and supernova ejecta, and ``smooth'' gas accreted from the intergalactic medium. We find that recycled gas dominates the accretion budget and is already metal rich at early epochs. Gas from other origins typically undergoes gradual chemical enrichment within the galactic environment prior to black hole accretion. The mean abundance ratios show only weak redshift evolution and are broadly compatible with the high metallicities inferred for quasar broad-line regions. Our results suggest that metal-rich gas supply to SMBHs arises naturally from cosmological galaxy evolution and stellar recycling.

AI.tldr: This study uses 30 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations to trace the origin and chemical enrichment of gas accreted by supermassive black holes in massive galaxies. The gas is classified into four categories (early, external, recycled, and smooth), with recycled gas found to dominate the accretion budget and be already metal-rich at early epochs. Accreted gas shows weak redshift evolution in abundance ratios and is consistent with quasar broad-line region metallicities, suggesting metal-rich SMBH feeding arises naturally from galaxy evolution and stellar recycling.
AI.motivation: Understanding the origin and chemical properties of gas accreted by supermassive black holes is essential for linking black hole growth to galaxy evolution, as this connection remains poorly understood.
AI.method: The study employs 30 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of massive galaxies (stellar masses 10^10.9-11.9 Msun, black hole masses 10^8.5-9.7 Msun at z=0). Individual gas particles are traced through their full cosmological histories to identify origins and enrichment pathways, classifying accreted gas into four categories: early, external, recycled (from AGB winds and supernova ejecta), and smooth (from the intergalactic medium).
AI.result: Recycled gas dominates the SMBH accretion budget and is already metal-rich at early epochs. Gas from other origins undergoes gradual chemical enrichment within the galactic environment before accretion. Mean abundance ratios show weak redshift evolution and are broadly compatible with high metallicities inferred for quasar broad-line regions.
AI.conclusion: Metal-rich gas supply to SMBHs arises naturally from cosmological galaxy evolution and stellar recycling, without requiring special enrichment mechanisms.

title: Automatic detection of fast oscillations of dark matter scalar field and updated cosmological constraints on QCDM
comment: 28 pages, 6 figures and 3 tables
summary: It is well known that a scalar field dark matter with a quadratic potential undergoes fast oscillations when the time period represented by the mass scale in the Klein-Gordon equation becomes much smaller than that set by the Hubble parameter. This makes a solution to the equation numerically intractable. Many works in the literature have addressed the problem by either switching between solving the Klein-Gordon equation in the well-behaved regime to solving the fluid equations at the onset of oscillations, or by introducing a new set of variables that can absorb these oscillations. Despite being successful, these techniques rely on an estimate of when the oscillations start. For large scale scans of a model's parameter space, this can become cumbersome. Furthermore, the techniques have been used mainly for non-interacting dark matter models. In this work, we introduce an averaging technique with an automatic detection of the onset of oscillations, capable of capturing the non-interacting as well as the interacting dark matter scenarios. The technique, implemented in \texttt{CLASS}, is tested on the QCDM model and shows excellent detection and averaging abilities. We also update the cosmological constraints on the model using the most recent public data.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an averaging technique with automatic detection of the onset of oscillations for solving the Klein-Gordon equation in scalar field dark matter models, handling both non-interacting and interacting scenarios. The technique is implemented in CLASS and tested on the QCDM model, with updated cosmological constraints from recent public data.
AI.motivation: Solving the Klein-Gordon equation for scalar field dark matter with a quadratic potential becomes numerically intractable when fast oscillations occur (mass scale period << Hubble parameter timescale). Existing methods require manual estimation of oscillation onset, which is cumbersome for large parameter space scans and have mainly been limited to non-interacting dark matter models.
AI.method: The authors introduce an averaging technique with automatic detection of the onset of oscillations, capable of handling both non-interacting and interacting dark matter scenarios. The technique is implemented in the CLASS Boltzmann solver code.
AI.result: The technique is tested on the QCDM (quadratic potential dark matter) model and demonstrates excellent detection and averaging capabilities. The authors also update cosmological constraints on the model using the most recent public data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed averaging technique with automatic oscillation-onset detection provides a robust and efficient solution for scalar field dark matter simulations across both interacting and non-interacting regimes, eliminating the need for manual oscillation-onset estimation while delivering updated cosmological constraints on the QCDM model.

title: Why is GN-z11 Bright, Compact, and Nitrogen Enhanced? Insights from UV Absorption and Emission Diagnostics
comment: 22 pages, 11 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: We investigate the UV spectrum of GN-z11, a luminous, compact galaxy with strong nitrogen lines, at $z=10.60$, using deep JWST/NIRSpec high-resolution IFU and medium-resolution MSA spectra assembled from the JADES, SPURS, and GO programs. After optimized reduction and extraction of the IFU data including an evaluation of statistical and systematic uncertainties, we obtain mutually consistent spectra from the high- and medium-resolution observations. After carefully accounting for the data quality limitations, we identify prominent P-Cygni profiles in NV$λ\lambda1238,1243$, SiIV$λ\lambda1394,1403$, and CIV$λ\lambda1548,1550$, together with broad NIV]$λ\lambda1483,1486$ emission (FWHM $\sim1600$ km s$^{-1}$). The P-Cygni profiles resemble those of massive stars such as O-type stars and luminous blue variables (LBVs), while the broad NIV] emission resembles that of nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) stars. We fit stellar and active galactic nuclei (AGN) UV spectral models and find that the stellar models are strongly preferred over the AGN models ($Δ$WAIC $=-25$), with the preference driven primarily by the NV P-Cygni profile. These results indicate that the luminous, compact UV continuum of GN-z11 is dominated by massive stars. We derive electron densities from CIII]$λ\lambda1907,1909$, NIII]$λ\lambda1747-1754$, and NIV], with the nitrogen diagnostics extending well beyond the CIII]-based limit and reaching densities of $\gtrsim10^{6.5}$ cm$^{-3}$ for NIV], indicating physically distinct carbon- and nitrogen-emitting nebular components. These findings suggest that the apparent nitrogen enhancement inferred for GN-z11 as a whole may arise when strong narrow nitrogen emission originates from dense gas locally enriched in nitrogen by WN stellar winds and photoionized by nearby massive stars within the same star-forming region.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra of GN-z11 (z=10.60) and finds that its strong nitrogen lines and UV continuum are dominated by massive stars (O-type, LBVs, and WN stars) rather than an AGN. The nitrogen enhancement is attributed to dense, locally nitrogen-enriched gas from WN stellar winds photoionized by nearby massive stars, not an overall abundance enhancement.
AI.motivation: GN-z11 is a luminous, compact galaxy at z=10.60 with strong nitrogen lines, and it is crucial to determine whether its UV emission is powered by massive stars or an AGN, and to explain the apparent extreme nitrogen enhancement observed in this early galaxy.
AI.method: Assembly and optimized reduction of JWST/NIRSpec high-resolution IFU and medium-resolution MSA spectra from JADES, SPURS, and GO programs. Statistical and systematic uncertainties were evaluated, and stellar vs. AGN UV spectral models were fitted (using WAIC model comparison). Electron densities were derived from CIII], NIII], and NIV] nebular diagnostics.
AI.result: P-Cygni profiles in NV, SiIV, and CIV (massive-star-like) plus broad NIV] emission (WN-star-like) were identified. Stellar models were strongly preferred over AGN models (ΔWAIC=-25). Electron densities reach ≳10^6.5 cm^-3 from NIV], indicating distinct carbon- and nitrogen-emitting components.
AI.conclusion: The UV continuum of GN-z11 is dominated by massive stars, and the apparent nitrogen enhancement is likely local: dense gas enriched by WN stellar winds and photoionized by nearby massive stars within the same star-forming region, rather than a global abundance increase in the galaxy.

title: The Most Probable Outer Density Profile from Excursion Set Theory
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures
summary: Measurements of the turnaround radius around galaxy clusters can be used to break the degeneracy between measurements of the present day energy density of matter and dark energy. Korkidis & Pavlidou showed that the turnaround radius coincides with the first point of deviation between outer density profiles in N-body simulations and the analytic profile predicted by excursion set theory. However, their analytic profile relied on a number of simplifying assumptions, which may each introduce systematic error. We evaluate the effect of these assumptions on the shape of the analytic profile and its correspondence with simulated outer density profiles. We relax the key simplifying assumptions and re-derive the mode of the outer density profile from excursion set theory. We then numerically resolve the double distribution (DD) across a range of masses and clustering parameters, and compare the numerical mode estimate to the re-derived analytic profile. We find excellent agreement between our analytic profile and the numerically-realized DD. However, our analytic profiles diverge from N-body profiles, and this divergence grows as we relax successive assumptions. We relate this mismatch to the differing window functions used in the analytic and simulation-based approaches, which respectively yield Markovian and correlated density trajectories. We conclude that the analytic profile proposed by Korkidis & Pavlidou should only be used as a few-parameter effective description of the most-probable outer density profile, with parameters fitted to results of cosmological simulations.

AI.tldr: The authors evaluate the simplifying assumptions in Korkidis & Pavlidou's analytic excursion set theory profile for the turnaround radius around galaxy clusters. They relax these assumptions, re-derive the analytic profile, and compare it to numerical double distribution (DD) solutions and N-body simulations. While the analytic profile matches the numerical DD, it diverges from N-body profiles increasingly as assumptions are relaxed, due to differing window functions producing Markovian vs. correlated density trajectories. The analytic profile should only be used as a fitted effective description.
AI.motivation: The turnaround radius around galaxy clusters can break degeneracy between matter and dark energy density measurements. However, the analytic profile used to define this radius rests on simplifying assumptions that may introduce systematic errors, undermining its reliability for cosmological inference.
AI.method: The authors relax the key simplifying assumptions in Korkidis & Pavlidou's excursion set theory framework, re-derive the mode of the outer density profile analytically, numerically resolve the double distribution (DD) across a range of masses and clustering parameters, and compare the numerical mode to the re-derived analytic profile as well as to N-body simulation results.
AI.result: Excellent agreement is found between the re-derived analytic profile and the numerically-realized DD. However, analytic profiles diverge from N-body profiles, with divergence growing as successive assumptions are relaxed. The mismatch is attributed to differing window functions: analytic approaches yield Markovian density trajectories while simulations yield correlated ones.
AI.conclusion: The analytic profile of Korkidis & Pavlidou should not be used as a first-principles prediction; instead, it should serve as a few-parameter effective description of the most-probable outer density profile, with parameters fitted to cosmological simulation results.

title: FLAGS II: Constraining Galaxy Formation Models with Dimensionality Reduction of Direct Observables
comment: 18 pages, 10 figures. Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Comparisons between observations of galaxies and theoretical predictions are regularly performed using physical properties, which are inferred by the often slow and biased process of SED fitting. Forward modelling facilitates a reliable alternative, whereby models are evaluated using direct observables alone. However, these datasets become high-dimensional when collating observations from multiple telescopes, leading to sparse sampling, memory intensity and visualisation difficulties. We show that 2D embeddings of JWST and HST photometric fluxes, constructed using the non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm UMAP, preserve sufficient information to differentiate between five models. Using a simple $χ^{2}$-like metric, we show that JAGUAR reproduces the population of bright galaxies $(m_{\mathrm{AB}}<26)$ in GOODS-S six times as well as SC-SAM and twelve times as well as SAGE. By adjusting the hyperparameters, we quantify how well each model replicates the distribution of SED shapes. The template SED approach of SPRITZ and the lack of photoionisation in SAGE cause significant discrepancies, highlighting the importance of comprehensive forward modelling. The embedded position of each galaxy can be identified $>100$ times faster than inferring its properties with Bayesian SED fitting, making this approach an ideal alternative for deriving statistical model constraints from large surveys such as LSST and Euclid, and performing simulation-based inference with CAMELS.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that 2D UMAP embeddings of JWST and HST photometric fluxes can serve as a fast, direct alternative to SED fitting for comparing galaxy observations to theoretical models. The approach differentiates between five forward models, finds JAGUAR reproduces bright galaxies in GOODS-S six times better than SC-SAM and twelve times better than SAGE, and identifies galaxies over 100x faster than Bayesian SED fitting.
AI.motivation: Traditional SED fitting for comparing galaxy observations to theoretical predictions is slow and biased, while forward modelling with direct observables produces high-dimensional datasets that are sparsely sampled, memory-intensive, and difficult to visualize when combining data from multiple telescopes.
AI.method: The authors apply the non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm UMAP to construct 2D embeddings of JWST and HST photometric fluxes, then use a chi-squared-like metric to quantitatively compare how well five forward models (JAGUAR, SC-SAM, SAGE, SPRITZ, and another) reproduce the observed distribution of SED shapes. Hyperparameters are adjusted to quantify model fidelity.
AI.result: UMAP embeddings preserve sufficient information to differentiate between five models. JAGUAR reproduces the population of bright galaxies (m_AB<26) in GOODS-S six times as well as SC-SAM and twelve times as well as SAGE. Template-based SPRITZ and SAGE's lack of photoionisation cause notable discrepancies. Embedded galaxy positions are identified over 100 times faster than Bayesian SED fitting.
AI.conclusion: The UMAP-embedding approach is an ideal alternative for deriving statistical model constraints from large surveys like LSST and Euclid, and for performing simulation-based inference with CAMELS, offering significant computational speedups without loss of discriminatory power.

title: Higher-Order Analytical Expansion of Thawing Dark Energy with an Exponential Potential
comment: 22 pages, 3 figures
summary: Motivated by recent DESI results suggesting dynamical dark energy, we investigate the thawing scenario in quintessence with an exponential potential, $V=V_0e^{-λφ/m_{\mathrm{pl}}}$, by analytically expanding the deviation of the equation of state parameter $w_φ$ from $-1$ in powers of $λ$. In addition to the previously known leading-order result at $O(λ^2)$, we derive the $O(λ^4)$ correction as a function of the density parameter $Ω_φ$. We show that a consistent determination of the redshift dependence of $w_φ$ through $O(λ^4)$ requires corrections to the background expansion. We obtain the required correction by expanding $Ω_φ$ in powers of $λ$ around its $Λ\mathrm{CDM}$ value. Comparison with numerical solutions demonstrates that the $O(λ^4)$ expansion provides a more accurate approximation than the leading-order result. Our analytical approximation, which consistently incorporates the $O(λ^4)$ correction, will provide a potentially useful tool for distinguishing the exponential quintessence model from other dark energy models in future observations.

AI.tldr: The paper derives an O(λ⁴) analytical approximation for the equation of state parameter w_φ in thawing quintessence with an exponential potential, extending the previous leading-order O(λ²) result. The authors show that consistent O(λ⁴) accuracy requires corrections to the background expansion, obtained by expanding the density parameter Ω_φ around its ΛCDM value. Numerical comparisons confirm the improved accuracy of the O(λ⁴) expansion.
AI.motivation: Recent DESI observations suggest dynamical dark energy, motivating a more precise analytical description of the thawing quintessence scenario to distinguish it from other dark energy models.
AI.method: Analytically expand w_φ in powers of λ for the exponential quintessence potential V=V₀e^{−λφ/m_pl}. Derive the O(λ⁴) correction as a function of Ω_φ, and compute background corrections by expanding Ω_φ in λ around its ΛCDM value. Validate against numerical solutions.
AI.result: The O(λ⁴) expansion provides a significantly more accurate approximation than the leading-order O(λ²) result when compared to numerical solutions. The authors demonstrate that background expansion corrections are necessary for consistent redshift-dependent predictions at O(λ⁴).
AI.conclusion: The improved O(λ⁴) analytical approximation will serve as a useful tool for distinguishing exponential quintessence from other dark energy models in upcoming observational analyses, particularly in light of DESI's dynamical dark energy hints.

title: Trace the Self-Gravitating Gas Using CO Isotopologues
comment: 23 pages, 14 figures, accepted by ApJ
summary: Recent studies have shown that the star formation rate (SFR) correlates tightly and linearly with the mass of gravitationally bound gas, which can be delineated from the power-law tail of the column-density probability distribution function ($N$-PDF) derived from dust emission observations. This relationship holds across four orders of magnitude within the Milky Way--spanning low-mass to high-mass star-forming regions and encompassing the extreme environment of the Central Molecular Zone. Building on this framework, we present a new approach for estimating the mass of gravitationally bound gas in molecular clouds using multi-line CO isotopologue observations. Our sample includes 16 molecular clouds with robust detections in $^{12}$CO, $^{13}$CO, and C$^{18}$O $J$ = 1-0, spanning both massive inner Galaxy clouds and nearby star-forming regions. We find that the $N$-PDFs derived from combined CO isotopologue data recover the characteristic log-normal plus power-law profiles seen in dust-based studies. The mass and spatial distribution of the self-gravitating structures estimated from both dust-based and CO-based methods agree well throughout the sample. This indicates that the CO isotopologue combination can robustly trace the self-gravitating component via the $N$-PDF method and provides a reliable, scalable, and velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission for identifying the star-forming gas in molecular clouds.

AI.tldr: The authors present a new CO isotopologue-based method to estimate the mass of gravitationally bound gas in molecular clouds by constructing N-PDFs from combined 12CO, 13CO, and C18O J=1-0 observations. Across 16 molecular clouds spanning the inner Galaxy and nearby star-forming regions, they show that CO-derived N-PDFs reproduce the log-normal plus power-law structure seen in dust-based studies, and that the mass/spatial distribution of self-gravitating gas agrees well with dust-based estimates, offering a scalable, velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission.
AI.motivation: To provide a reliable, scalable, and velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission for tracing self-gravitating gas in molecular clouds, building on the established tight linear correlation between SFR and the mass of gravitationally bound gas derived from the power-law tail of dust-based N-PDFs.
AI.method: Construct N-PDFs from combined CO isotopologue (12CO, 13CO, C18O J=1-0) data for 16 molecular clouds spanning massive inner Galaxy clouds and nearby star-forming regions, and compare the resulting log-normal plus power-law profiles, masses, and spatial distributions of self-gravitating structures against dust-based estimates.
AI.result: CO isotopologue-derived N-PDFs recover the characteristic log-normal plus power-law shape seen in dust-based N-PDFs, and the mass and spatial distribution of self-gravitating structures from CO-based and dust-based methods agree well across the entire sample.
AI.conclusion: The CO isotopologue combination robustly traces the self-gravitating component via the N-PDF method, providing a reliable, scalable, and velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission for identifying star-forming gas in molecular clouds.

title: Gaia parallax bias via spherical harmonics: A Python tool and discussion of possible causes
comment: Submitted. The parallax-correcting code in Python and graphical presentation is available at https://zenodo.org/records/21708614
summary: Parallaxes in Gaia DR3 are known to suffer from a complex set of sky-correlated and magnitude-dependent offsets or biases at the level of a few tens of $μ$as. Estimated from a sample of one million distant quasars and AGNs from the CRF catalog, the average offset is negative, but the actual distribution of this important parameter shows significant variations on the sky. We propose a practical method to evaluate the parallax correction as a function of sky position and, optionally, of $G$ magnitude using a spherical harmonic series, and supply a tested Python tool {\tt varpi3.py} available on Zenodo\footnote{ https://zenodo.org/records/21708614}. We find that only the constant $Y_{00}$ term is significantly dependent on magnitude, while the other 80 harmonic terms are either close to zero or flat with magnitude. The directions of the smallest and largest parallax offsets are $(l,b)\simeq(220\degr,+43\degr)$ and $(l,b)\simeq(45\degr,-45\degr)$, which are close to the orientation of the quasar density dipole reported in recent publications. Motivated by this curious coincidence, we review possible physical effects resulting in a negative bias of measured parallaxes, including an anisotropic universe with a positive curvature and an orbital aberration component. The proposed method of parallax correction is tested using independent asteroseismology data for four different areas on the sphere. Finally, we show that the parallax zero-point propagates into the CRF proper-motion field through the parallax--proper-motion covariance, biasing the vector spherical harmonic determination of the secular-aberration glide, and hence the Galactocentric acceleration, at the microarcsecond-per-year level.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the sky-correlated and magnitude-dependent parallax biases in Gaia DR3 data (tens of μas level), proposing a practical spherical harmonic-based correction method via a Python tool (varpi3.py). The study finds only the constant harmonic term depends on magnitude, identifies the extreme offset directions correlating with the quasar density dipole, and demonstrates that uncorrected parallax zero-points bias CRF proper-motion fields and secular aberration determinations.
AI.motivation: Gaia DR3 parallaxes suffer from complex, sky-correlated and magnitude-dependent biases at the tens-of-microarcsecond level, which degrade astrometric measurements. A practical, accurate correction method is needed to account for these spatially varying systematics, and understanding the physical origin of these biases is important for extragalactic and Galactic science relying on precise parallaxes.
AI.method: The authors model the parallax correction as a spherical harmonic series in sky position with optional G-magnitude dependence. They estimate coefficients using parallax data from one million distant quasars and AGNs from the CRF catalog. A Python tool (varpi3.py) is supplied for implementation. The correction is validated against independent asteroseismology data in four sky regions, and the propagation of the parallax zero-point into CRF proper motions via the parallax–proper-motion covariance is analyzed.
AI.result: Only the constant Y00 term shows significant magnitude dependence; the other 80 harmonic terms are near zero or magnitude-flat. The smallest and largest parallax offsets occur near (l,b)≈(220°,+43°) and (l,b)≈(45°,−45°), aligning with the quasar density dipole orientation. The method is validated using asteroseismology data, and it is shown that the parallax zero-point biases the vector spherical harmonic determination of secular aberration glide and hence Galactocentric acceleration at the μas/yr level.
AI.conclusion: The proposed spherical harmonic-based parallax correction provides a practical and tested solution for the sky-correlated systematic biases in Gaia DR3. The connection between parallax offset directions and the quasar density dipole motivates further investigation into physical mechanisms (e.g., anisotropic universe with positive curvature, orbital aberration). Correcting the parallax zero-point is essential not only for accurate parallaxes but also for unbiased proper-motion fields and secular aberration determinations.

title: CLASSY. XV. Kinematics and Spatial Distributions of Outflows in Local Highly Star-Forming Galaxies
comment: Accepted to ApJ, 15 pages, 5 figures
summary: Star-forming galaxies drive massive outflows that play an important role in galaxy evolution by regulating feedback and influencing the dynamics of surrounding media. Measuring galactic outflow rates is essential for quantifying feedback efficiency and the amount of mass, momentum, and energy deposited into the circumgalactic medium. In this paper, we examine 17 galactic outflows from the CLASSY survey with radiative transfer modeling of UV absorption lines presented in M. Huberty et al. (2024), to study their spatial distributions and kinematic properties. We study the SiII, SiIII, and SiIV ionization states that trace the cool and warm phases of the outflows and find that SiII traced winds generally behave differently than the warmer SiIII and SiIV traced winds. We derive the mass, momentum, and energy loading factors, which we find scale inversely proportional to stellar mass. We find that our measurements of the mass and momentum loading factors are in agreement with the hydrodynamic FIRE-2 simulations. We model the velocity profiles of the winds, with profiles reaching a maximum velocity of 620 km/s on average, in agreement with hydrodynamic simulations from CGOLS. We also investigate the relationship between outflow properties and the age of the stellar population from SED fitting. We find that outflows associated with young star forming regions are more likely to have a column density dominated by cooler gas and have mass outflow rates which decrease with radius.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes 17 galactic outflows from the CLASSY survey using radiative transfer modeling of UV absorption lines to study their spatial distributions and kinematic properties, finding that SiII-traced winds differ from warmer SiIII/SiIV-traced winds, deriving loading factors that scale inversely with stellar mass and agree with FIRE-2 simulations, and connecting outflow properties to stellar population ages.
AI.motivation: Quantifying galactic outflow rates is essential for understanding galaxy evolution, feedback regulation, and the deposition of mass, momentum, and energy into the circumgalactic medium, requiring detailed observations and modeling of outflow properties.
AI.method: Radiative transfer modeling of UV absorption lines (SiII, SiIII, SiIV) for 17 galactic outflows from the CLASSY survey, combined with SED fitting to derive stellar population ages and comparisons with hydrodynamic simulations (FIRE-2 and CGOLS).
AI.result: SiII-traced winds behave differently from warmer SiIII/SiIV-traced winds; mass, momentum, and energy loading factors scale inversely with stellar mass; mass and momentum loading factors agree with FIRE-2 simulations; wind velocity profiles reach a maximum of 620 km/s on average, in agreement with CGOLS; outflows from young star-forming regions are more likely dominated by cooler gas with mass outflow rates decreasing with radius.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a detailed characterization of galactic outflow properties across multiple ionization phases, demonstrates consistency with state-of-the-art hydrodynamic simulations, and reveals that the age of the stellar population influences the thermodynamic and kinematic structure of the outflowing gas.

title: Ripples in the OCEANS: Broad Line Variability of Little Red Dots
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a unique class of compact, red sources discovered in the JWST extragalactic deep fields. Determining if they are indeed powered by accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is one of the main drivers of the intense study of these objects. Evidence for variability in these objects provides a direct test for the active galactic nucleus (AGN) nature of their central engine. In this study, we present a variability analysis of 6 LRDs observed by the $R \sim 2700$ OCEANS survey and leverage archival $R \sim 1000$ spectroscopic data from the CEERS and RUBIES surveys. We report marginal detections of $\rm Hα$ broad-line (BL) variability in the LRDs OCEANS-100424/RUBIES-42232 (27\% variability at 2.1$σ$ significance) and OCEANS-35829/RUBIES-49140 (GlimmIr/Irony; 50\% variability at 1.5$σ$ significance). The other 4 LRDs in our sample do not show evidence for BL variability, with a 1$σ$ upper limit of $4.8 \% - 30\%$ variability between their epochs of observations. We also find no evidence ($<1σ$) for continuum variability in our LRD sample. We compare our results to a sample of SDSS-RM quasars to determine the probability of our broad $\rm Hα$ variability detections. We find that the probability of reproducing 2 variable and 4 nonvariable quasars is $4.71\%$, corresponding to $\sim 2 σ$ departure from typical quasar variability. The detection of BL $\rm Hα$ variability in 2 LRDs provides some evidence for the AGN nature of these objects as opposed to pure scattering models.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes variability in 6 Little Red Dots (LRDs) using OCEANS survey data combined with archival CEERS/RUBIES spectroscopy, finding marginal broad Hα line variability in 2 LRDs (27% at 2.1σ and 50% at 1.5σ) and no continuum variability, providing some evidence for AGN-powered central engines in these compact red sources.
AI.motivation: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, red sources found in JWST deep fields, and determining whether they host accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is a major open question. Variability provides a direct test of the AGN nature of their central engines, distinguishing them from alternative models such as pure scattering.
AI.method: The authors performed a variability analysis of 6 LRDs using R~2700 spectra from the OCEANS survey and archival R~1000 spectroscopy from CEERS and RUBIES surveys. They measured broad Hα line and continuum variability between observational epochs, and compared their detection rates against a sample of SDSS-RM quasars to assess consistency with typical quasar variability.
AI.result: Marginal broad Hα variability was detected in 2 LRDs (OCEANS-100424/RUBIES-42232 with 27% variability at 2.1σ and OCEANS-35829/RUBIES-49140 with 50% variability at 1.5σ). The other 4 LRDs showed no BL variability with 1σ upper limits of 4.8%-30%. No continuum variability was found (<1σ). The probability of reproducing 2 variable and 4 nonvariable quasars in SDSS-RM is 4.71%, corresponding to ~2σ from typical quasar variability.
AI.conclusion: The detection of broad Hα variability in 2 LRDs provides partial evidence supporting the AGN nature of these objects, arguing against pure scattering models, although the significance is marginal and the overall sample behaves inconsistently with typical quasar variability.

title: Observing Co-Located Neutral and Ionized Gas-Phase Iron Depletion in the Magellanic Clouds
summary: Depletion is the observed phenomenon where gas-phase elemental abundances are reduced through accretion onto dust grains. We measure neutral gas-phase elemental abundances (S, Fe) in the Magellanic Clouds along 33 sightlines using high-resolution UV spectroscopy (HST/COS and HST/STIS), and compare them to ionized gas-phase abundances (S, Fe) adopted from the literature for six co-located H\,\textsc{ii} regions (with the furthest separation of $\lesssim3'$, 50 pc). Comparing S abundances show that S is minimally depleted in the H\,\textsc{ii} regions and surrounding diffuse ISM. However, we find that the gas-phase Fe abundances in H\,\textsc{ii} regions can be lower than those of the neighboring neutral ISM by 0.3 to 2 dex. This difference is likely an offset in the amount of Fe depleted into dust grains. As accretion of gas-phase Fe is likely not effective at the temperatures of the H\,\textsc{ii} regions, Fe depletion into solid form would have occurred in the dense atomic or molecular clouds prior to star formation. Stronger depletion in the H\,\textsc{ii} regions shows that Fe-bearing grains survive destruction in the first few million years following ionization. Our observations highlight that Fe depletion in H\,\textsc{ii} regions can be a useful tracer of Fe depletion in dense molecular clouds, which are challenging to observe directly via UV absorption.

AI.tldr: This paper measures neutral gas-phase S and Fe abundances in the Magellanic Clouds along 33 sightlines using HST/COS and STIS UV spectroscopy, comparing them to ionized gas-phase abundances from co-located H II regions. While S shows minimal depletion in both environments, Fe abundances in H II regions are 0.3-2 dex lower than in the surrounding neutral ISM, indicating stronger dust depletion. The authors conclude that Fe-bearing grains survive destruction shortly after ionization and that H II region Fe depletion can serve as a tracer of depletion in dense molecular clouds.
AI.motivation: To understand dust depletion processes in the Magellanic Clouds by comparing neutral and ionized gas-phase abundances of S and Fe, and to establish whether H II region Fe depletion can trace depletion in dense molecular clouds that are difficult to observe directly.
AI.method: High-resolution UV spectroscopy using HST/COS and HST/STIS to measure neutral gas-phase S and Fe abundances along 33 sightlines in the Magellanic Clouds, compared against literature ionized gas-phase abundances from six co-located H II regions (within ~50 pc separation).
AI.result: S is minimally depleted in both H II regions and the diffuse ISM. Fe abundances in H II regions are 0.3-2 dex lower than in the neighboring neutral ISM, revealing an offset in the amount of Fe depleted into dust grains. Stronger depletion in H II regions indicates Fe-bearing grains survive destruction in the first few million years following ionization.
AI.conclusion: Fe depletion in H II regions can be a useful tracer of Fe depletion in dense molecular clouds, since accretion onto dust must have occurred in cold, dense pre-star-forming gas rather than in the hot H II region environment, and the surviving grains demonstrate resistance to destruction in the early post-ionization phase.

title: SPURS: Massive Stars, Dense Gas, and Ly$α$ Escape in GN-z11 at $z = 10.6$
comment: Main text 35 pages, 20 figures
summary: We present ultra-deep {\it JWST} spectroscopy of GN-z11 ($z=10.6$) obtained through the SPURS Cycle 4 Large Program, providing the deepest rest-UV view yet obtained of a galaxy at $z>10$. GN-z11 was previously found to be nitrogen-enhanced with detectable Ly$α$. The SPURS spectrum reveals P-Cygni stellar wind features and broad He II emission that are jointly reproduced by stellar population models incorporating very massive stars (VMS; $>100\,M_\odot$) at low metallicity and young ages ($\lesssim3$ Myr). We also detect a broad ($\rm FWHM=1670$ km s$^{-1}$) component to N IV] $\lambda1486$, now seen in several nitrogen emitters, potentially arising from dense WN winds or LBV-like outbursts associated with a population of VMS in a dense environment, though an AGN-driven wind cannot be excluded. In either scenario, this broad component may trace the gas producing GN-z11's nitrogen enhancement. Rest-UV absorption lines reveal a fast ($\sim500$~km~s$^{-1}$), highly ionized outflow and a negligible neutral gas covering fraction. We resolve the weak Ly$α$ emission (EW=5.6 Å, $f_{\rm esc,Lyα}=2.7$\%), finding a broad red wing (44\% of flux at $>500$ km s$^{-1}$) that should experience reduced IGM damping wing suppression and help explain Ly$α$ visibility at $z>10$. Fine-structure O I* $\lambda1304$ emission indicates dense neutral gas near a subset of the ionizing sources, which may also scatter Ly$α$ to the large observed velocities. The weak low-ionization absorption favors a picture in which this dense neutral gas is confined to a compact nuclear region. Together, these results are consistent with a rapid burst of star formation building up the dense nuclear regions and surrounding clusters in GN-z11.

AI.tldr: Ultra-deep JWST SPURS spectroscopy of GN-z11 (z=10.6) reveals P-Cygni features and broad He II consistent with very massive stars (>100 M⊙) at low metallicity and young ages. A broad N IV] component and fast ionized outflow are detected, while weak Lyα emission shows a broad red wing that reduces IGM suppression. The results support a rapid starburst building dense nuclear regions.
AI.motivation: To obtain the deepest rest-UV view of a galaxy at z>10 and understand the physical conditions, stellar populations, outflows, and Lyα escape mechanisms in GN-z11—the most distant galaxy previously found to be nitrogen-enhanced with detectable Lyα.
AI.method: Ultra-deep JWST spectroscopy via the SPURS Cycle 4 Large Program; comparison of observed features (P-Cygni stellar wind features, broad He II, broad N IV] component, rest-UV absorption lines, Lyα and O I* emission) to stellar population models and kinematic/diagnostic analysis.
AI.result: Detection of P-Cygni and broad He II features reproduced by VMS models (young, low metallicity); broad N IV] component (FWHM=1670 km/s) potentially from dense WN winds or LBV-like outbursts; fast (~500 km/s) highly ionized outflow with negligible neutral covering fraction; weak Lyα (EW=5.6 Å, f_esc=2.7%) with 44% of flux at >500 km/s red wing; O I* emission indicating dense neutral gas near ionizing sources.
AI.conclusion: GN-z11 hosts a rapid burst of star formation containing very massive stars, building dense nuclear regions and surrounding clusters. Dense neutral gas is confined to a compact nuclear region, and the broad Lyα red wing explains its visibility at z>10 through reduced IGM damping wing suppression.

title: ALMA observations of pre-JWST z ~ 10 galaxy candidates: A CO(J = 9-8) line from a ULIRG at z = 2.54 and revisit of the photometric redshifts with JWST photometry
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures (7 in Appendices), MNRAS in press
summary: We present Atacama Large Millimetre/submillimetre Array (ALMA) observations targeting the [OIII]$88\,μ$m line for six $z\sim10$ galaxy candidates selected with the Hubble Space Telescope and the Spitzer Space Telescope. We detect a line ($4.5σ$) and dust continuum emission ($30σ$) in UDS_18697, while detecting neither robust line nor continuum emission in the remaining five objects. The detected line in UDS_18697 is identified as CO($J=9-8$), because follow-up James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) NIRSpec observations have confirmed the redshift as $z=2.54$. UDS_18697 is classified as an ultra luminous infrared galaxy (ULIRG) with far-infrared (FIR) luminosity of $L_\mathrm{FIR}\approx1.1\times10^{12}\,L_\odot$, assuming a dust temperature of $T_\mathrm{d}\approx42\,$K, estimated using a physically-motivated method. We find that UDS_18697 follows the $L_\mathrm{FIR}-L'_\mathrm{CO}$ relation for local and $z>2$ galaxies, albeit being slightly brighter in CO($J=9-8$). Also, based on the follow-up NIRSpec observations and spectral energy distribution fitting using JWST/NIRCam photometry, we found that most of our targets are suggested to be low-$z$ interlopers. Motivated by these redshift misclassifications, we investigate colour--colour selection criteria for high-$z$ galaxies using JWST spectroscopic survey catalogues. We find that elevating a colour threshold tracing the Lyman break is crucial for constructing a robust high-$z$ sample, particularly for wide field surveys such as Euclid Deep Fields and Roman High-Latitude Wide-Area Survey.

AI.tldr: ALMA observations targeting [OIII] 88μm in six z~10 galaxy candidates reveal that most are low-redshift interlopers, not true high-z galaxies. One object (UDS_18697) shows line and dust continuum emission but is confirmed by JWST/NIRSpec to be a z=2.54 ULIRG. The authors propose improved colour-colour selection criteria with elevated Lyman-break thresholds to construct robust high-z galaxy samples for future wide-field surveys.
AI.motivation: To test whether photometrically-selected z~10 galaxy candidates are genuine high-redshift sources, and to improve selection criteria for high-z galaxy identification in large-scale surveys given potential redshift misclassifications.
AI.method: ALMA observations of the [OIII] 88μm line for six z~10 galaxy candidates selected via HST and Spitzer photometry; follow-up JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy and NIRCam photometric SED fitting to confirm redshifts; analysis of CO(9-8) line, dust continuum, and FIR luminosity; empirical testing of colour-colour selection criteria using JWST spectroscopic survey catalogues.
AI.result: Only one object (UDS_18697) had detected line (4.5σ) and continuum (30σ) emission, which was identified as CO(9-8) at z=2.54 via JWST/NIRSpec. This object is a ULIRG with LFIR≈1.1×10^12 L⊙ (Td≈42K) and follows the LFIR-L'CO relation for local and z>2 galaxies. Most other targets were found to be low-z interlopers based on follow-up JWST observations. Elevating the Lyman-break colour threshold is critical for robust high-z sample selection in wide surveys like Euclid Deep Fields and Roman HLWAS.
AI.conclusion: Photometric z~10 galaxy candidates are prone to contamination by low-redshift interlopers. Higher Lyman-break colour thresholds are necessary for constructing reliable high-z galaxy samples in forthcoming wide-field surveys.

title: Gal3D: Superellipsoid Modeling of Radial 3D Galaxy Structure in IllustrisTNG and EAGLE Simulations
comment: 22 pages, 11 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ. Source code: https://github.com/GalaxySimAnalytics/gal3d, and data: https://osf.io/k9x3e/
summary: Galaxy morphology and structure are key tracers of galaxy formation and evolution, making accurate measurements of intrinsic three-dimensional (3D) shape essential for linking morphology to galaxy assembly and for comparing numerical simulations. We present Gal3D, a framework that reconstructs smoothed density fields from particle data and quantifies the radial 3D structure of simulated galaxies by fitting superellipsoids to iso-density surfaces. The method recovers axis ratios, orientations, center offsets, and superellipsoid indices ($S_a$, $S_b$, $S_c$), enabling a flexible characterization of diverse galactic structures such as disks, classical bulges, box/peanut bulges, and triaxial components. Applying Gal3D to galaxies in the IllustrisTNG and EAGLE simulations, we find that the radial extent of flattened disk regions increases with stellar mass up to $M_{*,30}\sim10^{11}\,M_\odot$ and then declines sharply, with EAGLE galaxies showing a saturation at $M_{*,30}\sim10^{10.5}\,M_\odot$. The bar-related $ \varepsilon_{ab}\equiv 1-b/a$ strengthens above $M_{*,30}\sim10^{10.5}\,M_\odot$ in both simulations, but remains systematically weaker in EAGLE. In TNG, outer bar regions are commonly associated with elevated $S_a$ and $S_c$, indicating enhanced boxiness and more prominent box/peanut-shaped bulges, whereas such higher-order signatures are weak or absent in EAGLE. At the highest stellar masses, flattened disks become less prominent, while inner prolate or triaxial structures remain common and massive EAGLE galaxies have more prolate or triaxial outer stellar bodies than their TNG counterparts. These results demonstrate that Gal3D provides a practical framework for quantifying intrinsic radial 3D structure and comparing morphology across cosmological simulations.

AI.tldr: Gal3D is a framework that reconstructs smoothed density fields from particle data and fits superellipsoids to iso-density surfaces to quantify the radial 3D structure of simulated galaxies. Applied to IllustrisTNG and EAGLE, it reveals mass-dependent trends in disk extent, bar strength, box/peanut bulge signatures, and triaxiality, with systematic differences between the two simulations.
AI.motivation: Galaxy morphology and structure are key tracers of formation and evolution, yet accurate measurements of intrinsic 3D shapes are needed to link morphology to galaxy assembly and to enable fair comparisons with numerical simulations.
AI.method: Gal3D reconstructs smoothed density fields from particle data and fits superellipsoids to iso-density surfaces, recovering axis ratios, orientations, center offsets, and superellipsoid indices (S_a, S_b, S_c). It is applied to galaxies in the IllustrisTNG and EAGLE cosmological simulations.
AI.result: The radial extent of flattened disks increases with stellar mass up to ~10^11 Msun then declines, with EAGLE saturating earlier at ~10^10.5 Msun. Bar-related epsilon_ab strengthens above ~10^10.5 Msun in both simulations but is systematically weaker in EAGLE. TNG shows elevated S_a and S_c in outer bar regions (box/peanut signatures) that are weak or absent in EAGLE. At the highest masses, flattened disks diminish while prolate/triaxial structures dominate, more so in EAGLE.
AI.conclusion: Gal3D provides a practical and flexible framework for quantifying intrinsic radial 3D structure of simulated galaxies and enables meaningful morphological comparisons across different cosmological simulations.

title: Radio Properties of Narrow-Line and Broad-Line Seyfert 1 Galaxies
comment: 33 pages, 13 figures, 11 tables. Published in Galaxies
summary: Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxies host active galactic nuclei (AGN) with narrow optical emission lines of the broad-line region. This is often explained with a relatively lower mass of the central supermassive black hole and super-Eddington accretion. We compared the radio properties of large samples of NLS1 and broad-line Seyfert 1 (BLS1) galaxies compiled from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. We cross-matched the NLS1 and BLS1 samples with the Faint Images of the Radio Sky at Twenty-Centimeters (FIRST) sky survey at 1.4 GHz and the first and second epoch data of the Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS) at 3 GHz. We calculated the radio spectral indices, the 1.4-GHz radio power, and the radio loudness. We found lower 1.4-GHz radio detection rates for the NLS1 galaxies. The median radio loudness values, the fraction of radio-loud AGN, and the median 1.4-GHz radio power are also lower for the NLS1 sample. The median spectral indices imply a slightly steeper radio spectrum for the NLS1 sample than for the BLS1 sample. Comparison of the star formation rates estimated from the radio data and the infrared measurements of the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer satellite indicated that more than half of the FIRST- and VLASS-detected NLS1 and BLS1 galaxies contain radio-emitting AGN.

AI.tldr: This study compares the radio properties of large samples of narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) and broad-line Seyfert 1 (BLS1) galaxies drawn from SDSS, cross-matched with FIRST (1.4 GHz) and VLASS (3 GHz) surveys. NLS1 galaxies exhibit lower radio detection rates, lower radio loudness, a smaller fraction of radio-loud AGN, lower 1.4-GHz radio power, and slightly steeper radio spectral indices compared to BLS1 galaxies. Radio-infrared comparison shows more than half of radio-detected galaxies in both samples host radio-emitting AGN.
AI.motivation: NLS1 galaxies show evidence for lower black hole masses and super-Eddington accretion, yet their radio properties relative to BLS1 galaxies remain poorly characterized. This work aims to systematically compare the radio emission properties of large NLS1 and BLS1 samples to better understand the radio-AGN connection in these sources.
AI.method: Large NLS1 and BLS1 samples from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) were cross-matched with the FIRST survey at 1.4 GHz and first and second epoch VLASS data at 3 GHz. Radio spectral indices, 1.4-GHz radio power, and radio loudness were computed. Star formation rates were estimated from radio data and compared with WISE infrared measurements to separate star formation from AGN radio emission.
AI.result: NLS1 galaxies show lower 1.4-GHz detection rates, lower median radio loudness, a lower fraction of radio-loud AGN, and lower median 1.4-GHz radio power than BLS1 galaxies. The NLS1 sample exhibits slightly steeper radio spectra. Radio-infrared comparison indicates that more than half of the FIRST- and VLASS-detected NLS1 and BLS1 galaxies contain radio-emitting AGN.
AI.conclusion: The radio emission properties of NLS1 galaxies are systematically weaker and slightly steeper spectrally compared to BLS1 galaxies, consistent with their lower black hole masses and super-Eddington accretion scenario. Most radio-detected Seyfert 1 galaxies host genuine radio-emitting AGN rather than purely star-formation-dominated radio emission.

title: Differential Reddening and Extinction Law Analyses of Galactic Open Clusters
comment: 15 pages, 9 figures, 1 table, Accepted for publication in AJ
summary: Extinction significantly affects open cluster parameters and their use in studies of Galactic structure, yet homogeneous large sample measurements of open cluster extinction properties remain limited. Using Gaia-era open cluster member samples combined with multi-band photometry and stellar parameters, we derive color excesses of member stars and provide the homogeneous characterization of the mean reddening, differential reddening, and color excess ratio (CER) at the cluster scale. Differential reddening increases systematically with mean reddening, with highly reddened clusters near the Galactic plane showing stronger extinction variations. Star-by-star reddening corrections narrow color--magnitude diagram (CMD) sequences in 369 of 435 clusters (85%) with reliable CMD-width measurements, and cluster color excess maps reveal small-scale extinction structures. The median CER is compatible with the standard diffuse interstellar medium extinction curve, while the broad CER distribution and its large-scale variations across the Galactic disk likely reflect differences in the dominant dust environments sampled along different Galactic sight lines.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a homogeneous, large-sample characterization of extinction properties (mean reddening, differential reddening, and color excess ratio) for open clusters using Gaia-era member samples and multi-band photometry, finding that differential reddening scales with mean reddening, star-by-star corrections improve CMDs in most clusters, and the median color excess ratio matches the standard interstellar extinction curve with variations reflecting different dust environments across the Galactic disk.
AI.motivation: Extinction significantly affects open cluster parameter estimates and their use in Galactic structure studies, yet homogeneous large-sample measurements of open cluster extinction properties remain limited.
AI.method: The authors combine Gaia-era open cluster member samples with multi-band photometry and stellar parameters to derive per-star color excesses, enabling homogeneous measurements of mean reddening, differential reddening, and color excess ratios at the cluster scale, as well as cluster color excess maps.
AI.result: Differential reddening increases systematically with mean reddening, with stronger extinction variations in highly reddened clusters near the Galactic plane. Star-by-star reddening corrections narrow CMD sequences in 369 of 435 clusters (85%). The median color excess ratio is compatible with the standard diffuse interstellar medium extinction curve, while the broad CER distribution and large-scale variations across the Galactic disk reflect different dust environments along different sight lines.
AI.conclusion: This study provides a homogeneous, large-sample extinction characterization for open clusters, demonstrating that differential reddening correlates with mean reddening near the Galactic plane, that per-star reddening corrections effectively improve cluster CMDs, and that color excess ratio variations trace differences in the dominant dust environments encountered along different Galactic sight lines.

title: Widefield Arecibo Virgo Extragalactic Survey: II. Characterizing the HI properties and environment of the WAVES South region
comment: 16 pages + 4 pages of appendices, accepted in A&A, 14 figures, 4 tables
summary:
Context. Galaxy clusters are extreme environments where interactions with the hot intracluster medium drive rapid galaxy evolution. These processes can result in the formation of optically dark gas clouds, as previously observed in Virgo and other clusters.
  Aims. We investigate the distribution and properties of neutral hydrogen (HI) in two large adjoining regions of the Virgo cluster to understand how the cluster environment influences galaxy transformation. Specifically, we examine the gas content of both star-forming and quiescent populations and search for evidence of gas-loss driven evolution.
  Methods. We cataloged the 21cm HI Widefield Arecibo Virgo Extragalactic Survey (WAVES) South data using visual and automatic source extraction methods. By combining these results with an optically selected sample, we compared the HI properties of WAVES South with the previously studied VC1 region. To probe gas reservoirs below the nominal detection limit, we performed a stacking analysis of radio spectra across the WAVES South, VC1 and VC2 footprints.
  Results. We detected 56 HI sources with a median root mean square (rms) noise of 0.8 mJy, including 50 galaxies, two gas clouds (one being optically dark), and the ALFALFA Virgo 7 complex. Our results reveal a significantly lower detection fraction in WAVES South compared to the VC1 region. Stacking showed no new HI detection at a 0.080 mJy rms with a maximum of 157 stacked objects from WAVES South, VC1, and VC2.
  Conclusions. The lower HI detection fraction suggests that WAVES South is a more dynamically relaxed and evolved environment than the VC1 region. The presence of residual HI in a small subset of early-type galaxies supports a model of dwarf irregular to dwarf elliptical transformation via environmental stripping. Finally, we note a possible evolutionary link between optically dark clouds and recently discovered "blue blobs."

AI.tldr: This study catalogs HI sources in the WAVES South region of the Virgo cluster using the Arecibo telescope, detecting 56 sources including 50 galaxies and two gas clouds. Compared to the VC1 region, WAVES South shows a significantly lower HI detection fraction, indicating a more dynamically relaxed and evolved environment. Stacking analysis found no new HI detections, and the study suggests evolutionary links between optically dark clouds, early-type galaxy transformation, and recently discovered "blue blobs."
AI.motivation: To understand how the Virgo cluster environment drives galaxy transformation by investigating the distribution and properties of neutral hydrogen (HI) across two large adjoining cluster regions, and to probe gas-loss driven evolution in both star-forming and quiescent galaxy populations.
AI.method: Cataloged 21cm HI data from the WAVES South survey using visual and automatic source extraction methods, combined with an optically selected sample for comparison with the VC1 region. Performed stacking analysis of radio spectra across WAVES South, VC1, and VC2 footprints to probe gas reservoirs below the nominal detection limit.
AI.result: Detected 56 HI sources at a median rms of 0.8 mJy, including 50 galaxies, two gas clouds (one optically dark), and the ALFALFA Virgo 7 complex. A significantly lower detection fraction was found in WAVES South compared to VC1. Stacking to 0.080 mJy rms (up to 157 stacked objects) revealed no new HI detections.
AI.conclusion: WAVES South is a more dynamically relaxed and evolved environment than VC1. Residual HI in a subset of early-type galaxies supports a dwarf irregular to dwarf elliptical transformation model via environmental stripping. A possible evolutionary link exists between optically dark clouds and recently discovered "blue blobs."
